evidence.summary: Table 1 reports parameter, FLOP, measured throughput, and six-dataset zero-shot classification results for four original/pruned/distilled CLIP encoders.
Table 2 shows that distilled compressed CLIP encoders match or slightly exceed original mean recall on Flickr30K and COCO.
Table 4 reports DINOv2-g at 0.62B parameters and 0.16T FLOPs with distilled kNN accuracy equal to the 83.5% original.
Table 3 compares AMP against five pruning baselines at comparable size on OpenCLIP-g and EVA-CLIP-E.
Table 5 reports 53.8% average pruning-only accuracy for information entropy versus 50.0% for cross entropy, despite a slightly smaller model.
Table 6 reports 53.8% average accuracy for binary search versus 7.3% for uniform Taylor pruning, a 46.5 percentage-point gap.
Equations 5-7 construct a label-free possibility distribution from class-token similarities and compute its mean entropy.
Equation 8 directly matches teacher and student class and patch tokens, explaining why the reported recovery is a post-distillation result.

edges.rationale: All four reported CLIP encoders show roughly 36-43% parameter/FLOP reduction and distilled average accuracy within 0.3 points of the original.
Retrieval results extend near-lossless recovery beyond classification for the CLIP-style models.
DINOv2-g recovers its original kNN accuracy after a 45.6% parameter reduction.
The equation explains the recovery mechanism but does not itself demonstrate accuracy.
The measured ratios are approximately 1.47x, 1.50x, 1.61x, and 1.45x for the four CLIP encoders.
The ablation supports better downstream pruning accuracy, but does not measure importance-score accuracy directly and covers one backbone.
The equations establish that all inter-instance possibilities contribute and no labels are required.
The result directly favors adaptive sizing over uniform sizing, but only for one backbone and the prose contains a conflicting numerical claim.
AMP also exceeds several alternative pruning strategies at matched model size.
The criterion uses only backbone class-token representations and therefore does not require labels or a prediction head.
DINOv2-g is an explicit end-to-end demonstration of head-free pruning and recovery.

sufficiency_checks.rationale: Tables directly report size, compute, and task performance.
The gold claim is restricted to evaluated backbones, tasks, and post-distillation recovery.
Every compressed model is compared with its original counterpart.
The overall compression/recovery claim is a main outcome rather than a component attribution claim.
Evidence spans multiple model scales, datasets, and three evaluation families.
Accuracy variance and significance are not reported.

limitations: Near-lossless applies after distillation; pruning-only EVA accuracy degrades sharply.
No accuracy uncertainty estimates are reported.
claim_assessments.rationale: Multiple direct tables support the carefully scoped claim.

sufficiency_checks.rationale: Table 1 reports measured images per second.
The claim retains the exact hardware, batch, resolution, and model scope.
Each pruned encoder is paired with its original throughput.
No component attribution is claimed.
Only one GPU configuration and batch size are tested.
Ten runs are averaged but no variance is reported.

limitations: The result should not be generalized to other hardware, latency-sensitive batch sizes, or DINOv2-g.
claim_assessments.rationale: Direct measurements support the explicitly scoped roughly-1.5x claim.
